lessons.title: Hello, Rust!
lessons.concept: A familiar beginning, a few new details
body: A Rust program starts in fn main(). Braces define its body, and statements usually end with a semicolon.
println! is a macro—the ! is the clue. It formats text and adds a newline. Let’s give the compiler something to work with.
lessons.task: Print exactly Hello, Rust! to the console.
lessons.hint: Change the text inside the double quotes.

lessons.title: Make room for change
body: Rust makes reassignment an explicit choice. A binding created with let cannot be assigned a new value unless you opt in with mut.
The starter produces E0384. Read the compiler’s suggestion, then make x mutable. This changes the value without changing its type.
lessons.task: Keep the reassignment, make x mutable, and print 10.
lessons.hint: Write let mut x = 5; to allow the later assignment.
